All your VRChat haptics, in one app. OscGoesPurrr (OGP) reads the contacts on your VRChat avatar and turns every touch into real-time output on your devices: Bluetooth toys: Lovense, We-Vibe, Kiiroo and anything else Buttplug.io supports. Shockers: PiShock and OpenShock, over the hub's USB cable. Suits and more: bHaptics and OWO suits, SteamVR trackers with a motor, and the PlayStation VR2 headset's rumble. Friends can drive all of it over the internet, from their own OGP or from a link in their browser. You decide what each of them may use. It's one file for Windows, and an AppImage for Linux. The toy server is built in, and OGP finds VRChat and your toys by itself: no IPs, no ports. Home: two toys, the shocker hub, both suits and the headset, each with its quick switches. The sidebar on the left has the modes, total strength, Off and Sleep.

A Windows PC (10 or 11), or Linux. Bluetooth for your toys. VRChat with OSC switched on. An avatar with SPS contacts (VRCFury's sockets and plugs; older OGB and TPS setups work too). That's the standard toy setup. Optional: VRCFury in your avatar's Unity project, for OGP's own menu.

Getting started: from download to your first buzz, step by step. Toys: Home, the Toys page, modes and strength, where the toy server runs, and anti-stuck and Sleep. Your avatar: OGP's menu in your avatar, the parameters OGP sends back, and SPS 3 avatars. Shockers: the hub, the safety rules, behaviours and ShockOSC avatars. Friends: adding friends, what each may do, driving them, groups, the web remote and VRChat accounts. Avatar Remote, Suits and trackers, PSVR2, Records and Settings and tools. Common problems: what goes wrong, why, and what to do. tip OGP explains itself too. Rest the mouse on anything in the app to see what it does, or press F1 on any page for its steps on top of the page.

The Avatar Remote is VRC Parameter Relay's board, built into OGP: your avatar's parameters as toggles, hold buttons, sliders and steppers, sorted into coloured categories. You use it, your avatar's menu can use it, and friends you allow can use it too. Switch it on first: Settings → Features → Avatar Remote — avatar boards friends can use too, or tick An avatar remote friends can use too in What are you here for?. It's off by default. Its page is My Avatar Remote. My Avatar Remote: the worn avatar's board with its categories, the Height box, and the parameter list on the right.

Wear your avatar, with VRChat's OSC on. Its board opens by itself. Press ＋ Category for a box to put controls in. Each category has a colour. Open the parameter list with Avatar parameters ◂. Double-click a parameter, or drag it onto a category, to make a control. The kind follows the parameter's type: a toggle for a Bool, a stepper for an Int, a slider for a Float. ⋯ → Edit on a card changes its label, its kind or its range, or inverts a toggle (⇄, for a parameter whose logic is backwards). An Int can be several toggles or hold buttons too, each setting its own value (Outfit = 1, 2, 3 …, shown as =2 on the card). They switch each other off, like VRChat's own menu.

Drag a card by its ⠿ to move it, and a category by the ⠿ in its header. To remove a control, drag it back onto the parameter list. The list lights up with Drop to remove; the control goes at once, with Undo for a moment. A whole category asks first. Ctrl+Z takes back any change to a board.

Every avatar keeps its own board. Give it a name in Avatar name and it stays in the ▾ list, so you can edit its board while you wear something else. ✎ OFFLINE then means nothing is sent. An avatar can have several presets: the drop-down at the top. ⋯ next to it adds, renames and deletes them. A category's ⋯ copies it to another preset. ⟳ Resync reads the avatar's parameters again.
A category's 🔒 makes it look-only for friends. You can still use it, and so can your own avatar menu.
Built boards in VRC Parameter Relay already? Import from VRC Parameter Relay… copies them all. The Relay's own files stay as they are.

Friends whose Avatar box is ticked in your friend list see the board of the avatar you're wearing, under your toys on their Friends page, and can use it. Everything they do is logged. They see your worn avatar's active preset, never one you opened for offline editing. A locked category (🔒) is look-only for them. Friends looking, at the top of My Avatar Remote, shows who has your board open right now. Nothing is sent to a friend until they have your board open. Then only changes.
On a friend's panel, THEIR AVATAR is their worn avatar's board, if they use the Avatar Remote and let you. Press a toggle, hold a button, move a slider. A locked category says look only.

⚡ YOLO hands every friend you allow every parameter of the avatar you wear, not only your board (VRChat's own, like Viseme, aside). Locks don't hold for them then. It asks before it goes on, and stays on until you switch it off. One switch for everyone.

Untick a friend's Avatar box: they lose your board. Pause all on the Friends page blocks every set, and lets go of any button a friend holds. A button a friend holds is let go when their updates stop. The web remote gets your board only once you tick its Avatar switch.

The Height box on My Avatar Remote changes your height in VRChat, the way the OSC scaler tools do. It sits under your categories. The Height box: your height now (1.42 m), the slider, Grow, Right away and Reset. Its top bar has the menu slot, the lock, ⋯ and its switch. Your height now: your eye height, live from VRChat. The slider picks the height to go to, between your lowest and highest. Grow glides there, gently. Right away jumps. Reset takes you back to your own height: what VRChat reported before anyone changed it.

⋯ in its top bar folds out: Lowest height and Highest height: the smallest and tallest anyone can make you, you included. By default VRChat's own menu range, 0.2–5 m. Never past 0.1–100 m, where VRChat warns things can break. Grow speed: how long Grow takes to double or halve your height. Slower is gentler on VRChat's view. Nobody else can change these.

Friends you allow your Avatar see the box on their copy of your board, and can change your height. The box's own switch (Height for friends, on by default) takes it away from them: they don't see it, and nothing they send changes your height. 🔒 makes it look-only for friends. Pause all holds it, like everything else. When a friend stops or leaves, your height stays where they put it. The circle in its top bar puts your height on one of your avatar menu's seven radials.
A world can forbid changing your height. The box then greys out and says so. A world's own limits win over what you set.

The avatar menu has OscGoesPurrr ▸ Avatar Remote: seven Toggles and seven Radials. Each is a slot you give a control, or a whole category, on the My Avatar Remote page. Then you use your board from VRChat's own menu.

Click the small circle in a card's top bar (or a category's). A radial opens like VRChat's: Back at the top, 1–7 clockwise, each saying what has it now. Click a number: the control takes that slot, from whatever had it. The circle then shows the slot's number. Click a number it already has to free it. A category can sit in both sets: the middle of the picker switches between Toggles and Radials. Back, Esc or a click elsewhere closes the picker. Toggles take toggles and hold buttons. A hold button is held while the toggle is on. Radials take sliders and steppers, across each one's own range. A slot holds one thing; one thing can take several slots. A category's slot drives every control in it that fits. The Height box takes a Radial. Slots are kept per preset. The menu drives the board of the avatar you're wearing, and it follows the board: a toggle is on while any of its controls is on, a radial sits where its first control is. note VRChat can't show the names (they're baked in when you upload), so the menu says Toggle 1–7 and Radial 1–7. The page shows what has each. Your own menu ignores locks: they're for friends. Parameter Type What it does OGP/Remote/Toggle1–7 Bool On / off for the slot's controls; a hold button is held while it's on. OGP/Remote/Radial1–7 Float 0–1 The slot's sliders or steppers, across each one's own range.

OGP tells your avatar whether each toy, suit and shocker is connected, so the avatar can light an icon, swap a material or switch an object on. They're plain Bool parameters, all on by default, under fixed names an avatar asset can count on. Settings → Connection Settings, with Tell VRChat while any toy is connected. What Where you set it Default name True while Any toy Settings → Connection Settings → Tell VRChat while any toy is connected OGP/ToyConnected at least one toy is connected One toy Toys → the toy's card → Avatar parameters → Tell VRChat while this toy is connected OGP/<ToyName>Connected, like OGP/LovenseLush3Connected that toy is connected bHaptics suit Suits → bHaptics → Tell VRChat → Any part OGP/BHapticsConnected at least one part is connected One bHaptics part the same card, a row per part you have OGP/BHapticsVestConnected, …SleevesConnected, …HandsConnected, …FeetConnected, …HeadConnected that part is connected OWO suit Suits → OWO → Tell VRChat OGP/OWOConnected OGP is connected to My OWO Any shocker Shockers → Hub → Tell VRChat while a shocker is connected OGP/ShockerConnected the hub is connected and a shocker is in use One shocker Shockers → the shocker's card → Tell VRChat OGP/Shocker1Connected, OGP/Shocker2Connected … numbered like the cards the hub is connected and that shocker is On PSVR2 headset PSVR2 → Tell VRChat while the headset is connected OGP/PSVR2Connected the headset is connected Each one can be renamed or switched off where it's listed. The suits', shockers' and headset's are only sent while that feature is on.

Add a Bool with the same name to your avatar's Expression Parameters. Unsynced is fine if only you need to see it; synced if others should. Drive whatever you like from it in your FX layer. A parameter your avatar doesn't have is ignored by VRChat. Two things with the same name share one parameter: true while either is connected. A Float or Int parameter gets 1 and 0. OGP sends them again every time you change avatar or VRChat reconnects, and sets them all to false when you close it. So an avatar never shows a device that's gone.

Settings → Connection Settings → Send thrust counters to VRChat (off until you switch it on) sends three counters as Int parameters, the same numbers as the Statistics page: Counter Parameter Counts Digits Total OGP/Thrusts/Total every thrust on record /D1 … /D7 Session OGP/Thrusts/Session since OGP started /D1 … /D5 Pace OGP/Thrusts/PerMin thrusts in the last 60 seconds /D1 … /D3 An avatar Int holds 0 to 255, so the plain parameter stops at 255. For a number display, use the digits: each is an Int 0–9, /D1 the ones, /D2 the tens, and so on. OGP/Thrusts/Total/D3 is the hundreds of the total. Add only the ones your asset uses; synced costs 8 bits each. Only changes go out, at most once a second. With Usage statistics off there's nothing to count, so nothing is sent.

OGP's controls can live in your avatar's own menu, so you never leave VRChat: strength, Off, Sleep, Test and the modes, a Friends submenu that drives whoever you picked in OGP, and the Avatar Remote's slots. Settings → VRChat menu: the three parts of the menu, whether the avatar you wear has them, and the download.

You need VRCFury in your avatar's Unity project (Creator Companion → Manage Project → add VRCFury). Download OscGoesPurrr-VRCFury.unitypackage (Settings → VRChat menu → Get the menu prefabs does the same) and import it into your avatar's Unity project. Drag one of its prefabs from the new Assets/OGP folder onto your avatar, anywhere inside it: OscGoesPurrr Menu: everything, your own controls and the Friends menu, in one OscGoesPurrr submenu. OscGoesPurrr Menu (Self): only your own controls (Avatar Remote included). OscGoesPurrr Menu (Friends): only the Friends menu, as an OGP Friends submenu. Upload. VRCFury adds the parameters and the submenu when you upload. The parameters are unsynced, so they cost 0 sync bits. Your avatar's own menu and parameter files aren't touched: to take it out again, delete the object. The submenu lands in your root menu. To put it in another submenu, type that submenu's name into the Prefix field of the prefab's Full Controller. A newer package imports over the old one and updates it in place. No VRCFury? The setup guide has a one-click installer for Unity and the manual way.
Settings → VRChat menu says, for the avatar you wear, which of the three parts it has: Your own controls, Friends submenu, Avatar Remote submenu. The Friends page says it too.

Parameter Type What it does OGP/Strength Float 0–1 Total output strength. Never touches your tuning. OGP/Mode Int 0–3 The active mode: 0 Combined, 1 Separate, 2 Custom 1, 3 Custom 2. Renaming a mode doesn't change its number. OGP/Off Bool Panic silence. Off again and your level comes back. OGP/Sleep Bool Toys wake only after three full strokes within six seconds. OGP/Test Bool, held While held, every connected motor runs at about 20 %. The menu and the app agree both ways: a change in OGP shows in your menu. After you load an avatar, OGP sends its own values; for about two seconds it ignores what VRChat replays then. So an avatar swap never changes your settings.

It acts on whatever you picked on the Friends page: a friend, or a group. Each friend only gets what they allow you. To drive yourself and a friend at once, put yourself in a group with them (see Groups and Me). Toys ▸: a level (OGP/Friend/Level), an auto mode (Sine, Square, Triangle, Saw, Random, Heartbeat, Build-up, Oscillate) with its speed and range, Override, which of their toys 1–4, and a stop. Shockers ▸: Shock, Shocker vibrate and Beep buttons, strength and length as a part of their caps, PiShock's Small warning, which shockers 1–4, and a stop. A shock is a vibrate while they haven't armed. Their strength: their total output strength slider. It moves on their screen too. Every parameter is listed in the setup guide.

Seven toggles and seven radials (OGP/Remote/Toggle1–7, OGP/Remote/Radial1–7) that you hand out to controls on the My Avatar Remote page. See Menu slots. tip Added the menu to an avatar you've used before, and nothing happens when you tap it? VRChat keeps an old list of the avatar's parameters. See Common problems.

VRCFury 1.1443.0 (November 2026) brought SPS 3. It renamed the zones' parameters (OGB/Socket/… and OGB/Plug/…) and measures depth with VRChat's newer contact receivers. OGP reads SPS 3 avatars as they are: nothing to set up, and your zones show in a toy's Select Zones like before. Older SPS, OGB and TPS avatars behave exactly as they always did.

Touch on an SPS 3 avatar is two things at once: how close the contact is, in the chain's Depth channel, plus VRChat's measured hand speed, in the Speed channel. The chain's Combine stage mixes them, as it does for penetration. So a still hand resting on you feels different from a stroking one. Penetration depth comes from the socket's depth contacts and the plug's length.

An SPS 3 avatar keeps its plug and socket touch receivers off until an app switches them on with OGB/Enabled. OGP sends it every few seconds and right after an avatar loads, next to the older OGB_ENABLED. You don't need to do anything; if your zones never show, see Common problems.

documents.t: Friends link two OGPs over the internet, so each can drive the other's toys, shockers and avatar, as far as the other allows. There's no account and no server of ours: the two PCs talk directly, with free relays as a fallback when a direct line isn't possible. Friends is on by default (Settings → Features → Friends — control each other over the internet). Nothing goes online until you pick a nickname. The Friends page: your nickname and Online at the top, the friend list, and the picked friend's panel below.
Type it into the box at the top. That's the name your friends see. Then OGP goes online, and the Online switch beside it is remembered from then on. Switch it off to go offline.

Press ＋ Add a friend (they need OGP too). It opens by itself while you have no friend yet. Under SEND AN INVITE LINK, pick how long it works: Once: the first friend who clicks it, within a day; 1 day / 1 week: anyone who clicks it in that time; No end: anyone who clicks it, until you close it. Press Copy invite link and paste it into Discord. It's a link that works in a browser too, with "(Add your name on OscGoesPurrr)" under it. Your friend clicks it, OGP opens on their PC, and you're friends.

Under the link is your ID, with Copy. A friend pastes it under GOT THEIR LINK OR ID? and presses Add; you press Accept when they ask. Your ID stays the same every time you open OGP. It's not a password: someone who has it can only ask to be your friend.

⋯ next to Copy invite link: Close all invite links: every link you sent stops working. Your friends stay. New ID - unfriend everyone…: for a link that got out of hand. Every friend is unlinked, and every link and your old ID stop working.

The list: you first, then your friends with their ping (Rin is offline, with ↻), your VRChat instance, and your groups. You are always first: the Me row, "this PC". See Groups and Me. Each friend shows their ping while linked, or offline. The three columns are what each friend may use: toys, shockers, your avatar. See What each friend may do. Click a friend to open their panel below. See Driving a friend.

OGP looks for offline friends in the background, gently, so the link stays light. To look right away: ↻ on an offline friend's row looks for that friend now; ↻ Check all next to FRIENDS looks for everyone who shows offline. The row says checking… until they answer or the try gives up. Each friend is looked for at most once every 10 seconds, however often you click.

Each OGP tells its friends its version. The first time a friend's is newer than yours, OGP says how to update, and an amber banner stays on the Friends page. A friend on an older version gets an OLD tag on their row.
At the bottom of a friend's panel: Unfriend name…. The other side drops you too. note One OGP per PC goes online. A second OGP window on the same PC stays offline.

Click a friend in the list and their panel opens below it: their toys, their shockers and their avatar, as far as they allow you. Mika's panel: their toys, their Collar as PiShock's panel, and the board of the avatar they wear.
ONLINE · direct · 18 ms: linked, and how. DRIVING YOUR TOYS: they're driving yours right now. +1 OTHER: someone else drives them right now. Hover for the names. Control mode and Pop out: see below.

All their toys drives every toy they have at once; a card per toy drives that one. Off, Direct control (a slider) and Random, then the patterns: Sine, Square, Triangle, Saw, Heartbeat, Build-up and Oscillate. Higher (the default): their toy runs at the higher of your level and what their own avatar does. Override: your level replaces theirs. Their strength: their total output strength slider. It moves on their screen too; whoever moves it last wins. Their strength, their Off and each toy's output band still hold on their side. Your level drops to zero when your updates stop.

Sync with others is their choice, not yours (on by default): everyone driving them shares one set of toy cards, and they feel only the newest change. With it off, each of you drives on your own, and the highest level wins. Their panel says SYNCED or SEPARATE beside +1 OTHER.
