documents.t: Shocker buttons: PiShock | OpenShock, in the header of THEIR SHOCKERS, picks whose buttons you drive with: PiShock's own panel (the default) or OpenShock's card. It's one setting for every panel (each friend's, your own and every group's), and OGP remembers it. It only changes how the buttons look: the same press sends the same thing, and everything they allow you holds either way.
It feels familiar if you've used PiShock: Shock and Vibrate with their strength, Duration and Warning (None, Small 1–3 s, Mid 3–6 s, Long 6–9 s), Use Mode (Tap, Remote, Continuous), STOP and Beep.

Nova's three shockers with OpenShock's buttons. It feels familiar if you've used OpenShock: Intensity and Duration dials, then Sound, Vibrate and Shock. One Intensity goes for Vibrate and Shock, and each stops at its own most. The Duration runs from 0.3 s up to their longest pulse. A press runs for the Duration, and the button stays lit. Press it again to stop it. Stop all stops their shockers, even when they have only one. Live control​ LIVE, in the card's corner, swaps the dials for Live control: pick Sound, Vibrate or Shock, then hold and drag on the pad. The strength follows your finger until you let go, and the top is the most they allow you. Live control on the Collar: the strength follows the finger, the line shows the last three seconds. It holds their shocker like PiShock's Remote mode: their longest hold and the rest after it still apply. It stops when you let go, and when your link goes quiet.

Strength is a part of their limit: the slider's top is the most they allow you. Not armed · a shock arrives as a vibration means they haven't armed. What they don't allow you is greyed, and the card says why. Party: tick it on several shockers (one friend's, or everyone's in a group) to drive them from one panel: Sync (all at once), Random (one each press), or Round Robin (one after the other).
Under THEIR AVATAR: the board of the avatar they're wearing, if they use the Avatar Remote and let you. A locked category is look-only.
Control mode fills the page with the panel, big, for VR. Exit control mode puts it back. Control mode: Mika's toys and shockers, big enough to use with a VR pointer.

Pop out puts the panel, big, in a window of its own: OscGoesPurrr · Control. A VR overlay (XSOverlay, OVR Toolkit, Desktop+) can then show just that window. It follows whoever you pick on the Friends page. It keeps working with OGP's main window minimized or in the tray. Stay on top keeps it above other windows. It remembers its size and place. It never opens by itself at launch. Nothing in it opens a popup window, which an overlay wouldn't show. Close it, or press Back into the page, and the panel goes back.
The avatar menu's Friends submenu drives whoever you picked here: their toys, their shockers and their strength. A change on the page shows in the menu, and the other way round.
The Friends page's log has two views: As it happens (every line as it comes) and By person (a row per person with their last action; ▸ unfolds what they did). Whole log ▸ opens the Log page.

You're always first on your own list: you, "this PC". It's a working friend who may do everything, over a loop inside OGP instead of the network. Click it and you drive your own toys, shockers and avatar from the same panel your friends use. Every friend rule still holds for it: Pause all, your shockers' switches, arming and limits. It can't be removed, and your real friends never see it.

A group drives several people at once from one panel. Under GROUPS, press + Group and give it a Name. Drag a row from the friend list onto the group's row, or onto its members box. A friend can be in several groups. Click the group to open its panel. A group's panel: its members as chips, and their toys and shockers together. The panel lists the members as chips. × on a chip takes that person out. Delete group removes the group, not the friends. Each member still only gives you what they allow you.

Drag yourself into a group with a friend. You're a member like any other, so the group's panel, and your avatar menu's Friends submenu with the group picked, drive both of you: your own toys and shockers follow too, through your own shocker page, your limits and arming.
documents.s: You and a friend at once

documents.t: An OGP friend is a nickname they chose. Linking them to their VRChat account says "this OGP friend is that VRChat person". Then OGP can show who's with you in VRChat, and can let only those people drive you. The link stays on your PC. It's never sent to the friend or anyone.

Under the friend list, IN YOUR VRCHAT INSTANCE has the switch Read VRChat's log (off by default). With it on, OGP reads who's in your instance from VRChat's own log file, while VRChat runs, and shows them as chips.

Either: drag someone from In your VRChat instance onto a friend's row; or open the friend's panel and press Link… next to VRCHAT ACCOUNT. Pick from the people in your instance, or from your VRChat friends in VRCX. Their VRChat name then shows under their nickname, smaller, with in your instance while they are. Unlink on their panel undoes it. One VRChat account belongs to one friend: linking it to another moves it. OGP keeps the account's user id, so a new display name doesn't break the link. Your People statistics use one name for a linked friend.
Import from VRCX, in the picker, reads your VRChat friends from VRCX's database: only when you click, read-only, never written to. Without VRCX installed, the button says so.

Only friends in my instance (under Read VRChat's log, off by default) lets only friends who are in your VRChat instance right now drive you. It's checked on your PC from your own log: your location never leaves your PC. Switching it on also switches on Read VRChat's log. A friend who isn't with you shows not here on their row, and everything they send is refused like Pause, and logged. If they leave mid-session, their drive drops to zero at once. Their panel says "Not here". An unlinked friend counts as not here: their row says not here · link their VRChat account. Allow from anywhere, in a friend's VRChat account box, lets that friend in from anywhere. The web remote is blocked while this is on (a browser can't be in your instance), unless its panel's Allow the web remote anyway is on. Your own Me row is never blocked. warning With Read VRChat's log switched off while this is on, nobody is seen in your instance, so no friend can drive you. OGP says so under the switch.

Someone without OGP can still drive you: share your web remote link. Whoever opens it gets a friend's whole panel in their browser, the same as in the app: your toys with every mode, your shockers as PiShock's panel with Party Mode (or OpenShock's, with Live control, at their Shocker buttons switch), and your avatar's board. No OGP, no account.

On the Friends page, press Copy web remote link (no OGP needed). It's right under ＋ Add a friend. Paste it anywhere. It's a plain link that opens in a browser, with a line under it saying whose toys it drives. One link per OGP. Everyone on it shows under one Web remote row, right after you in the list. Click that row for its panel.

On the Web remote's panel, WHAT THEY MAY DO is for everyone on the link at once: Toys: on from the start. Levels, auto modes, Override and your strength slider. Shockers and Avatar: off until you tick them, because anyone with the link gets them. Everything a friend's drive obeys, the web remote obeys too: Pause all, your Off and strength, each toy's output band, arming and each shocker's limits, locked categories, zero when its updates stop. It's all logged.

ON NOW lists every browser on your link right now. Kick lets one go: it can't come back with your link. On switches the link off: nobody gets in, and everyone on it is let go. New link…: your link stops working and everyone on it is let go. Share the new one. Remove web remote… takes it away entirely. A dead, replaced or switched-off link tells the browser so. Privacy The web remote is never a friend or a contact, and it never hears your friends' names: who else drives you reaches it only as a count. The page always connects through n0's free relays; no server of ours is involved.
You decide, friend by friend, what they may use. Everything they do is logged.

Every friend's row has three boxes, under the column icons: Column Icon Lets them Toys the pink capsule drive your toys Shockers the yellow bolt use your shockers Avatar the green remote see and use your Avatar Remote board All three are on for a new friend. A click on a column's icon sets that column for every friend (off first, while any has it on). Your shockers also need Share with friends on: it's the switch for all friends at once, on Home and on the Shockers page. See how the switches stack.

Pause all, at the top of the Friends page, stops everything every friend sends: toys, shockers, avatar buttons, your height. It covers the web remote and your own Me row too. Switch it off and they can go on.

Sync friends, next to Pause all, is yours alone to choose, for everyone driving your toys: friends, the web remote and your own Me row. On (the default), they share one set of toy cards: what one of them sets moves on everyone's cards, and your toys play the newest change. Off, each drives on their own, and your toys follow whichever of them is higher. Their panels show SYNCED or SEPARATE and can't change it.

What a friend may do with your shockers is what each shocker allows on the Shockers page: its Up to … limits, its Shock, Vibrate and Beep switches, whether it's on, arming, and the rests. Every friend, every group, your own Me row and the web remote get exactly those. There is nothing to set per friend: change a shocker's limits on the Shockers page and it holds for all of them. The one split is your avatar versus friends: with Separate limits for friends on, all friends together get their own caps and timing. Their panel shows those limits: the sliders stop there, and what a shocker doesn't allow is greyed, with why.
documents.s: Your shockers: the same limits for everyone

documents.t: Whatever a friend may do, these stay yours: Your toys: a friend's level stays under your total output strength, your Off, and each toy's output band. It drops to zero when their updates stop. Your shockers: every shock goes through the same gate as your own: arming, limits and the rest. A friend can't widen any of them. Your avatar: a locked category is look-only for friends. Everything is logged, on the Friends page and the Log. Want only friends who are with you in VRChat? See Only friends in your instance.
From download to your first buzz. Each step takes a minute.

Download OscGoesPurrr-Windows.exe and run it. It's one file: nothing to install, Intiface is built in. Windows shows a blue "Windows protected your PC" box the first time, because the exe isn't code-signed. Click More info → Run anyway. On Linux, get the AppImage instead: see Linux. New versions install themselves. OGP tells you when there's one.

The first launch asks What are you here for? Tick what you have and what you want: What you have: Toys, A shocker, A bHaptics suit or sleeves, An OWO suit, Trackers that vibrate, A PlayStation VR2 headset. What you want: Play with friends over the internet, An avatar remote friends can use too, Statistics of my sessions, OSC Inspector (for avatar makers). Press Done. OGP shows the pages for what you ticked and hides the rest. Skip changes nothing. You can change it any time in Settings → Features. Then the guided tour starts. It lights up one control at a time and waits for you to do the real thing. Follow it, or press End tour and use these steps.

Switch your toy on. OGP's built-in engine finds it over Bluetooth by itself. Close the toy's own phone app first. A toy talks to one thing at a time. No toy yet? The Toys page has Scan now, which looks right away. Your toys paired with Intiface Central on a phone (or another PC)? That works too: see Where your toys connect.
In VRChat: Action menu → Options → OSC → Enabled. OGP finds VRChat by itself. The sidebar's VRChat row says CONNECTED once it does.

Your avatar needs SPS contacts: VRCFury's sockets and plugs, the standard toy setup. Older OGB and TPS avatars work too. Until everything works, Home's Getting started line shows where you are: Toy on · VRChat connected · Avatar has SPS · Avatar menu. A dot turns green when that part works, and the line goes away once the first three are green. The avatar menu is optional. Optional: drag OGP's VRCFury prefab onto your avatar, so strength, Off, Sleep and the modes are in your avatar's own menu. See The avatar menu.

On Home, click your toy's row. It opens on the Toys page. Click Input, then Select Zones: these are your SPS sources. All SPS hears every zone your avatar has. Or switch on only the ones you want. Back on Home, the four chips on the toy's row choose who it feels: Touch from Self or Others, Penetration from Self or Others. A new toy hears touch and penetration from others. A toy's row on Home: what drives it (Ring), the four chips, its battery, a live meter per motor, Mute and Test.

Press Test all on Home. Every connected toy buzzes for about a second. Total output strength in the sidebar turns everything up or down. It never touches your tuning. Off in the sidebar silences everything at once. If you feel it, you're set.

Have fun. When you want more: Tune how a toy feels: The Toys page. Control OGP from VRChat: The avatar menu. A shocker: The hub, and read Arming and limits first. Friends: Adding friends. Something not working? Common problems.
Something not working? Find it below. Most of the time OGP already says what's wrong: rest the mouse on the thing that looks off, or press F1.
documents.s: Common problems and how to solve them

documents.t: Cause: the exe isn't code-signed, so Windows doesn't know it yet. Solution: click More info → Run anyway. Windows asks only the first time.

Cause: a toy talks to one thing at a time. If its phone app (or another program) has it, OGP can't. Or this PC's Bluetooth is off. Solution: close the toy's own app, switch the toy off and on, and press Scan now on the Toys page. Check that Bluetooth is on. The sidebar's Intiface row should say CONNECTED.

Cause: OGP still uses its built-in engine, or the phone doesn't let others in. Solution: on the phone, switch on Listen on all network interfaces (and Broadcast Server Info via mDNS to be found without an address), and start the server. In OGP, Settings → Intiface Engine → switch off Use built-in Intiface engine, and type the phone's address if it isn't found. It needs Intiface Central 3.0 or newer. See Where your toys connect.
documents.s: OGP doesn't see the Intiface Central on my phone

documents.t: Cause: the toy doesn't listen to that contact: its zones don't include it, or its chips leave out that kind of touch. A touch from yourself is off for a new toy. Solution: on Home, check the toy's four chips (Touch / Penetration from Self / Others). On the Toys page, open the toy's chain → Input → Select Zones, and pick All SPS or the zone. Make sure the toy isn't on Mute.
documents.s: My toy doesn't react when I'm touched

documents.t: Cause: total output strength is at 0 (a menu radial parked at 0 looks exactly like this), you're AFK in VRChat, or Sleep is on. Solution: check the strength slider. The status bar says AFK: everything off while you're away. Sleep waits for three full strokes.
documents.s: Everything is silent, and Off isn't on

documents.t: Cause: that's Sleep working: nothing plays until three full strokes land within six seconds, so a brush can't wake it. Solution: switch Sleep off for normal play.

Cause: modes are routings, not strengths. If two modes route the same motors from the same zones, they feel the same. Solution: set them apart on the Toys page → the toy → Input, with the mode you want to change active.
Cause: toys differ. Solution: leave total strength alone. Trim that toy: Toys → the toy → its chain → Output → Gain. If it does nothing low down or is too much at the top, set Output → Range.
documents.s: One toy is much stronger than the rest

documents.t: Cause: VRChat sent the contact's last value and then nothing more. Solution: leave Anti-stuck on: the Toys page's, under Toy server, and the toy's own Anti-stuck chip on its bar. It stops a frozen value after 1 s, or eases off one held at 100 % after 10 s. The suits and the headset have their own on their pages.
documents.s: A toy keeps running after my partner left

documents.t: Cause: OSC is off in VRChat, or VRChat isn't running yet. Solution: in VRChat, Action menu → Options → OSC → Enabled. OGP finds VRChat by itself. OSC Diagnostics, under TOOLS in the sidebar, shows what OGP sees.
documents.s: The VRChat row doesn't say CONNECTED

documents.t: Cause: the avatar you're wearing has no SPS (or OGB / TPS) contacts, or VRChat hasn't told OGP about it: OSC is off, or VRChat keeps an old list of the avatar's parameters from before you added SPS. Solution: wear an avatar with SPS sockets or plugs, with the VRChat row saying CONNECTED. Added SPS to an avatar you used before? Reset VRChat's list as in The avatar menu does nothing. An SPS 3 avatar needs nothing else: OGP switches its receivers on. No SPS on the avatar? Build your own zones under SPS Sources.

Cause: VRChat keeps an old list of each avatar's OSC parameters. An avatar you used before you added OGP's menu still has the old one. Solution: close VRChat, delete the folder %USERPROFILE%\AppData\LocalLow\VRChat\VRChat\OSC\ (just that folder; VRChat makes it again), and load the avatar.

Cause: the avatar has both the VRCFury prefab and the older one-click installer's submenu, and VRCFury merged them. Solution: remove the "OscGoesPurrr" submenu the installer added to your expressions menu. Its parameters can stay.
documents.s: Every control shows twice in my menu

documents.t: Cause: it's from an older prefab. Driving yourself and a friend at once is a group with you in it now. Solution: drag in the newer prefab. See Groups and Me.
documents.s: My menu has a "Both of us" folder that does nothing

documents.t: Cause: the world you're in forbids changing your height. Solution: nothing to fix: it works again in a world that allows it.
documents.s: The Height box is greyed out

documents.t: Cause: shocks aren't armed. Until you arm them, every shock is a vibrate. The red words say Shocks not armed. Solution: switch on Arm shocks (Home's shocker row or the Shockers page) and answer Yes. Read Arming and limits first.

Cause: the other side doesn't allow it: Shock is switched off on that shocker, or Vibrate is off there and they haven't armed (an unarmed shock goes out as a vibrate). The card says which. Solution: ask them. It's their call.
documents.s: A friend's Shock button is greyed

documents.t: Cause: another program has the hub's port open (only one can), or the cable only charges. Solution: close other shocker apps, try another USB cable, and press ↻ next to the port.

Cause: the avatar's ShockOSC settings say intensity 0, or Paused. They and the behaviours keep the same values, so the behaviours' strength is 0 or they're switched off. Solution: turn the avatar's Intensity up or unpause it in its menu, or change the behaviours on the Shockers page: the avatar follows.
Cause: they're offline, or OGP hasn't looked for them yet. It looks in the background, gently. Solution: press ↻ on their row, or ↻ Check all.
Cause: one OGP per PC goes online. Solution: use the first window.
documents.s: My second OGP window won't go online

documents.t: Cause: Pause all is on; or Only friends in my instance is on while Read VRChat's log is off, so nobody is seen in your instance; or their switches are off. Solution: check the top of the Friends page and the friend's row. See VRChat accounts and your instance.

Cause: they have Only friends in my instance on, and you're not in their VRChat instance (or they haven't linked you). Solution: join them in VRChat, or ask them to link your account or allow you from anywhere.
Cause: the link was replaced (New link…), switched off, or that browser was kicked. Solution: ask for the new link. A kicked browser can't come back with the old one.
documents.s: The web remote link stopped working

documents.t: Cause: the bHaptics Player is running. A suit takes one connection at a time. Solution: close the bHaptics Player, then press Connect. Let go hands the suit back to the Player later.
Cause: the headset isn't jailbroken (the commands go through, the motor never moves), or the toolkit isn't one of its experimental builds. Solution: see PSVR2.
The System Log page (under TOOLS) has what OGP did and why. The issues on GitHub are the place to ask.

On Linux, OscGoesPurrr is one AppImage. Download OscGoesPurrr-Linux-x86_64.AppImage. Make it executable: chmod +x OscGoesPurrr-Linux-x86_64.AppImage, or Allow executing in its Properties. Run it. Bluetooth needs BlueZ running, which it is on most desktops. The toy server is built in, as on Windows. New versions install themselves: OGP swaps the AppImage file for the new one.
PSVR2 is Windows only: its toolkit is. It isn't offered on Linux. Show toys in SteamVR (the toys in SteamVR's device list) is Windows only for now.

The PlayStation VR2 headset has a rumble motor. OGP drives it from one contact on your avatar: a light touch is a slow thump, a full one a fast buzz. Switch it on first: Settings → Features → PSVR2 — the headset's rumble, through PSVR2Toolkit, or tick A PlayStation VR2 headset in What are you here for?. It's off by default, and Windows only. The PSVR2 page: the link to the toolkit, the rumble band, the contact that drives it, and Tell VRChat.

PSVR2Toolkit, one of its experimental builds (the stable release doesn't have what OGP talks to). You install it yourself; OGP never bundles it. Run it once so OGP can find it. A jailbroken headset. On a stock one the commands go through and the motor never moves. SteamVR running with the toolkit.

Start SteamVR with the toolkit. Link says when OGP is joined to it. Connect whenever SteamVR runs (on once the feature is on) does that by itself. Under Contact, press Pick… and choose the contact receiver on your avatar that drives it. A Haptic Pancake avatar has HapticHead. Press Feel it. Silent while the page says connected? The headset isn't jailbroken. Set the rumble band: Lowest and Highest. The motor does 10–25 Hz; 0 is off.

Off, total output strength, VRChat going silent, Off while away and its own anti-stuck (at the bottom of the Contact card, with its own times) all hold it back. If OGP stops sending, the motor stops within half a second. On on Home's headset row (or Stop on this page) stops it. Tell VRChat while the headset is connected sends OGP/PSVR2Connected.

The Log page keeps everything friends, the web remote, you and your avatar did to your toys, shockers and avatar, for 30 days. It shows while Friends or Shockers is switched on. The Log: a row per person with their last action, and every entry below, newest first.

who: a friend, you (Me), a web remote guest, a group, or Your avatar (your own shocker behaviours, by name); what: toys, a shock, vibrate or beep with its level and shocker, an Avatar Remote set, a link coming or going, a switch; and why, if something was held back ("shocks from them are switched off", "not here"). Where OGP sent less than was asked, the entry says what they asked for, with what went out and why in a muted line under it: "Mika: vibrate 30 · 2.0 s on Collar", then "Cut to 1.0 s: your longest pulse". Statistics count what went out.

Click a person in the list at the top for only what they did. Person also offers everyone but your avatar's own behaviours. The kind chips leave out what you don't need: only shocks, only toys … Time: the last hour, today, the last 7 days, or everything. Search the log: a name, a shocker, a toy. Entries with all of the words show. Clear log deletes the whole log on this PC, after asking. It can't be undone.

The Friends page's log card has two views: As it happens and By person (a row per person, last action first; ▸ unfolds what they did). Shocks stand out. Whole log ▸ opens this page. info The log is one file per day in OGP's settings folder, on your PC only. It's never sent to anyone: friends see only their own panel.

How much your gear gets used, and when. Statistics stay on your PC and are never sent to anyone, friends included. It's on by default (Settings → Features → Usage statistics). Switching it off stops recording and keeps what's recorded. Delete statistics…, right under the switch, deletes it all. Statistics: every session with its length, active time, thrusts and a sparkline. The running one says recording.

Each session with its length, active time, thrusts, who you were with, and a sparkline. Show more lists older ones. Click a session for its page: its timeline: each toy's intensity, thrusts per minute and which zones were touched; a Shockers lane: a mark for every shock, vibrate and beep, as tall as it was strong. Hover for when, how strong, how long, which shocker and from whom; its totals and an analysis: active time, thrusts, pace, your longest streak and your hottest five minutes, plus who drove you and what reached your shockers.
Totals since you started, and Fun facts. Suits and trackers get their on-time next to your toys once one has buzzed.
A heatmap of the hours you play, and a month calendar. ← and → page through the months.

Who your sessions were with, ranked by thrusts: sessions, active time, thrusts, peak pace, last time. Tag a session with who it was with: the whole session, or a stretch you drag out on its timeline. OGP can tag it for you while you're alone in an instance with one other person, from VRChat's own log. That's opt-in. A friend linked to their VRChat account has one name in both places.

Every shock, vibrate and beep that reached your shockers: how many, the strongest, and for how long. Lifetime or This session. From whom: shocks, vibrates and beeps by person, with your avatar's behaviours, your menu and Party Mode as rows of their own, and per shocker. By person: your avatar's behaviours one by one ("Touch zones · Neck"), what you sent yourself from your avatar menu or Party Mode, each friend and each web remote guest. Per shocker. How long friends drove your toys, and how many Avatar Remote controls they set. Keep friends' names (on by default): off, new entries count as "A friend". Forget names… folds the names already kept. Lifetime totals stay after the Log's 30 days.
The same numbers can go to your avatar as Int parameters, for a counter display. See Thrust counters.
Settings → Appearance changes how OGP looks. Everything changes as you pick it: nothing restarts. Settings → Appearance: Vibrant or Darker, the colour slider, and Other colours folded under it.

Vibrant (the default) draws every card, button and chip with an outline in your colour. Darker turns those outlines down to a faint hairline and deepens the blacks, so only what matters lights up. The layout is the same in both.

One slider turns everything that's green (frames, buttons, highlights, even the faint tint of the background) to the colour you pick. Brightness and contrast stay, so every colour reads as well as the green. The colours that mean something keep theirs: each toy's own colour, pink for the live signal, amber for warnings, red for errors. If your colour lands right on one of them, that one moves out of its way: pick pink, and the live signal turns green.

Other colours ▸ shows those colours, each with a slider: Auto (the default): it keeps its own colour, unless yours comes too close. Drag a slider to set it yourself. It then stays where you put it. Auto hands it back.

Some things have one icon, the same in every place OGP names them: toys are a pink capsule, shockers a yellow bolt, the Avatar Remote a remote in your colour, Friends two people in cyan, suits a vest in orange. The pages that are no kind of thing (Statistics, Settings, Help, the tools) have line art in the sidebar's own tone.

While VRChat says you're AFK, everything is off: toys, shockers, suits, trackers, the headset and friends' drives. When you're back, it all comes back by itself. It's on by default, in Settings → Safety → Off while you're away. Settings → Safety: Off while you're away, with VRChat's AFK, GoGo Loco's AFK button, and Also off while.

VRChat's AFK: VRChat's own AFK parameter. GoGo Loco's AFK button: GoGo Loco's Locomotion menu has an AFK button of its own. OGP sees it too. Also off while: parameters of your own choosing. ＋ Add parameter… picks one; while it's on, everything is off as well. × takes it off the list.

It holds the same Off as the sidebar's Off, without touching your Off switch. Your own Off stays as you left it. The status bar says why, for example AFK: everything off. Friends' drives are held as with Off. It only counts while VRChat runs. When VRChat closes, every away reason lets go.

OGP does a lot; you probably need part of it. Settings → Features, the first card in Settings, switches each part on or off. Settings → Features: Choose what you use…, and a switch per feature, each with its page's icon. A switched-off feature hides its sidebar entry and stops its background work. Switching it back on brings everything back as you left it. Usage statistics off keeps what's recorded. Delete statistics… deletes it. Feature Default Its page Intiface toy communication (Buttplug.io) on Toys OSC Inspector (debug view) on OSC Inspector Usage statistics on Statistics Shockers — PiShock / OpenShock (USB) off Shockers bHaptics — suit and sleeves over Bluetooth off Suits OWO — EMS suit through the My OWO app off Suits Trackers — vibrating trackers through SteamVR off Suits PSVR2 — the headset's rumble, through PSVR2Toolkit off (Windows only) PSVR2 Friends — control each other over the internet on Friends Avatar Remote — avatar boards friends can use too off My Avatar Remote The Log page shows while Friends or Shockers is on.

Choose what you use… opens the same question a new install asks at its first launch: tick what you have (WHAT YOU HAVE) and what you want (WHAT YOU WANT), then Done. Each choice is a feature switch. It starts from your switches as they are, so you never lose one you use. Cancel changes nothing. OGP asks it by itself only once: at the first launch of a new install.
OGP explains itself in four ways.
documents.s: Help, Show me around and the tour

documents.t: Rest the mouse on any control, heading or button and its explanation pops up. Move away and it's gone. Nothing to switch on first.

Press F1, or ? Show me around in the status bar, on any page: the page's steps appear on a strip above it; whatever you point at lights up, with its name and what it does. Clicks do nothing while it's on, except the sidebar's pages, so looking around never changes a setting. Esc leaves. The strip's Guide ↗ opens that page's part of this guide.

Help opens with a tile per page: its steps, Show me ▸, which opens that page with Show me around on, and Read more ↗, its part of this guide. Pages you switched off aren't listed. Open the guide ↗, next to Take the tour, opens this guide; so does Guide ↗ in the status bar, at the page you're on. The long manual is folded under Every part in detail. The Help page: Take the tour, and a tile per page with its steps and Show me.

The tour walks you through OGP for real, one step at a time. It lights the control to click and moves on when you've done the real thing: a toy connects, its card opens, a zone is picked. Switch your toy on. It lights up on Home as it connects. Open it, then Input, then Select Zones: your SPS sources. The four Touch / Penetration chips. Test, then Total output strength. Optionally, OGP's menu in your avatar. A short part for each thing you picked: shockers, suits, the headset, friends, the avatar remote. Only the lit control takes clicks. The strip above the page says which step you're on, with Skip this step (or Next) and End tour. Esc ends it too. No toy yet? The step says what to check, and Continue without a toy moves on. It never changes a setting by itself. Arming the shockers is look-only. A new install takes it right after What are you here for?. Take it again any time: Take the tour ▸ on the Help page, or Take the tour in Home's Getting started.

Changed something you didn't mean to? Ctrl+Z takes it back, wherever you are in OGP. Ctrl+Y steps forward again. OGP remembers your last five changes, for the whole window. It covers every setting: toys' chains and modes, the Shockers page, Avatar Remote boards, the Friends list and groups, Settings. The status bar says what it did, for example Undid: removed Ears from the Avatar Remote. A new change after an undo drops what you could still redo.

Undo takes back settings, never what already happened: a shock, a toy's level, a friend's drive, a message sent. Changes made by a friend, your avatar's menu or OGP itself aren't steps either. Only what you changed.

An undo that would arm your shockers, switch a shocker or one of its actions back on, widen what a friend may do, or raise a limit asks first, the same way doing it by hand does. See Arming and limits.

A behaviour says what one of your avatar's contacts does to your shockers. They're the cards under BEHAVIOURS on the Shockers page. Two behaviours: Touch zones (the neck drives the Collar, a thigh the Thigh shocker) and a Contact on Headpat that drives both.

Press ＋ Add behaviour and pick its kind. Pick its contact: type the parameter's name, or Pick one your avatar sends. Choose what it does (Vibrate, Shock or Beep) and how strong. Give it shockers: drag a shocker card's ⠿ onto the behaviour, or press its +. A behaviour can drive several shockers. × on a chip takes one off. A new behaviour drives no shocker until you give it one. Its switch turns it on and off; × deletes it. A shock from any behaviour is still a vibrate until you arm, and stays under each shocker's limits. The picker lists ShockOSC's parameters first, and keeps PhysBone states (…_IsGrabbed, …_Stretch) visible, since behaviours use them.

Several contacts, each driving its own shockers: the neck the collar, a thigh its shocker. One action, strength and length for all of them; each contact's row takes its own shockers. ＋ Add a contact adds a row.

One on/off contact at a fixed strength: Pulse once: one pulse each time it's touched, of the set Length. Touch for at least ignores a brush shorter than that. While touching: running for as long as it's touched.
A value from your avatar, usually a proximity contact, runs the shockers while it's above Starts above. The closer, the stronger: from Strength just past it to Strength at 1.

Several OnEnter contacts on one spot, each with a different Min Velocity on the avatar. The hardest hit that fired picks the strength, so a slap lands harder than a tap. Each tier is a contact and a strength.

A PhysBone, like a tail or an ear: While held: Nothing, Vibrate, Shock or Beep. When let go: one pulse (Vibrate, Shock or Beep), the harder the pull the stronger: from Strength at a slight pull to Strength at full stretch. Pick the PhysBone's _IsGrabbed or _Stretch parameter, or type its name. ShockOSC's PhysBones work this way.

Your own behaviours pick the strongest among themselves for each shocker. With friends holding the same shocker, the strongest hold plays, and a shock beats a vibrate. A behaviour skips a shocker whose action it uses is switched off, so another behaviour can have it. Everything your avatar does to your shockers is in the Log as Your avatar, with the behaviour's name.

OGP drives PiShock and OpenShock shockers through the hub's USB cable: no account, no internet, straight from your avatar's contacts to the shockers. It never uses the PiShock or OpenShock cloud. Switch it on first: Settings → Features → Shockers — PiShock / OpenShock (USB), or tick A shocker in What are you here for?. It's off by default. warning Read Arming and limits before you put a shocker on. Shocks go out as vibrates until you arm them. The Shockers page: the hub, a card per shocker with its limits, and the behaviours below.

Plug the hub into this PC by USB. On the Shockers page, leave the port on Find automatically (or pick one; ↻ looks for ports again) and press Connect. Connect when the app starts connects it every time from then on. The hub card: connected to a PiShock hub on COM7, with Arm shocks, Share with friends, Stop all and Tell VRChat.

The hub can run PiShock's own firmware or OpenShock's: PiShock's 2023 and Lite hubs can be reflashed with it, and so can a DIY ESP32 board with a 433 MHz transmitter (CaiXianlin or Petrainer collars). OGP finds out which when it connects. A PiShock hub lists its shockers itself. Each gets a card. OpenShock firmware keeps no list, so add each shocker yourself: ＋ Add shocker makes a card with a model and a fresh transmitter ID. To pair a collar, hold its power button until the light blinks fast, then press the card's Beep. A PiShock shocker counts as CaiXianlin.

One shocker's card: its On / Off switch, what it's allowed to do, its limits, Tell VRChat and the test buttons. The name: click to rename it. The number in front of it on your friends' panels is the card's place. On / Off: a switched-off shocker stops at once and nothing reaches it. Its card stays where it is, greyed, with only its switch lit. Behaviours, friends and the web remote don't see it. Allowed: Shock, Vibrate and Beep, each switched on or off for this shocker. See Arming and limits. Limits: Up to shock strength, Up to vibrate strength, Up to a pulse of. The most anything may send to this shocker. Nothing is sent from here. Tell VRChat: a Bool that's true while this shocker is in use. See "It's connected" parameters. Test: Beep, Vibrate, Shock send one short pulse each, under the shocker's limits. The button of an action you switched off rests. The Every shocker card holds the limits all shockers share: At least a rest of, Up to a hold of, Then a forced break of.

Stop all stops every shocker at once and refuses everything until you press Resume. It's the same setting as On on Home's shocker row. These stop the shockers at once too: Off in the sidebar, or OGP/Off from your avatar's menu; Off while you're away; the USB cable coming out; VRChat going silent.
Home's shocker row has Arm shocks, Share with friends and On: the very same switches as on this page. A click on the row opens this page.

A shock reaches a person, so every send goes through one gate in OGP, whoever sends it: your avatar, your menu, a friend, the web remote. These rules hold for all of them. The rules Shocks are vibrates until you arm them. Unarmed, every shock (yours or a friend's) goes out as a vibrate. Arming asks first. Nothing arms the shockers without a Yes from you. Limits only ever get stricter. Friends and your avatar can lower a shocker's limits, never raise them. ShockOSC's settings are a behaviour's own values: they never move a limit. A switched-off action never fires. A shocker with Shock switched off never shocks, whoever asks.

Arm shocks is on the Shockers page's hub card and on Home's shocker row. It's one setting, shown in both places: flip it in one and the other follows. Switching it on asks: the switch turns into Arm shocks? Yes / No, right where it is. No answer within 5 seconds, and it stays off. Switching it off never asks. Red words beside it always say Shocks armed or Shocks not armed. It's remembered when you restart OGP. A Ctrl+Z that would arm the shockers asks the same question. Your friends see whether you're armed: their panel says Not armed · a shock arrives as a vibration.

From everyone to one friend: On (the hub) → Arm shocks (real shocks) → Share with friends (friends at all) → each friend's own Shockers switch on the Friends page (and the web remote's). Off stops everything, whatever the rest say. Not shared, no friend sees your shockers at all.

Each shocker card has a Limits box, and the Every shocker card holds the shared ones. They're the most anything may send; nothing is sent from there. The engine applies them to every send. Limit For Default Range Up to shock strength each shocker 30 1–100 Up to vibrate strength each shocker 30 1–100 Up to a pulse of each shocker 1.0 s 0.1–15 s At least a rest of every shocker 0.5 s 0.1 s – 1 h Up to a hold of every shocker 10 s 1 s – 10 min Then a forced break of every shocker 2.0 s 0.5 s – 10 min After anyone's pulse, that shocker rests for everyone, you included. A stronger pulse may still cut in: a shock cuts into a vibrate or a beep whatever their strengths, a vibrate into a beep, and within one kind the stronger one. Even then the pulses in a row never last longer than one longest pulse. A hold that reaches the longest hold stops, and the shocker takes its forced break. Holds by several people count as one hold. No pulse goes in during that break either, and a hold waits until a pulse and its rest are over. A friend sends a part of your limit: their strongest is your Up to … (or the friends' own, with Separate limits for friends on), the same for every friend (see What each friend may do). Nothing in OGP's settings goes past 100 % strength or a 15 s pulse.

The Every shocker card's Limits box has one switch: Separate limits for friends. It's off by default. Off: one set of timing for everyone, and one count. A friend's long hold and its forced break hold your avatar's contacts back too. On: the three timing limits come twice. Your avatar (your behaviours, ShockOSC's behaviours and your avatar menu) keeps to the first set, Friends (every friend, Me and the web remote) to the second, and each is counted on its own. A friend's long hold never blocks your contact shocks, and the other way round. Friends' caps: with it on, the Friends set also has Up to shock strength, Up to vibrate strength and Up to a pulse of. They hold for every friend on every shocker and only ever lower a shocker's own: a friend gets the lower of the two. Your avatar keeps each shocker's own. The catch: with it on, your avatar's longest hold and a friend's can run back to back, without the forced break between them. Arming and each shocker's switches stay shared either way. The first time you switch it on, the friends' set starts as a copy of your current values (each cap at the highest any shocker has), so nothing changes until you move one. Friends' panels show the caps and the longest hold they get. Separate limits for friends on: your avatar's timing, then the Friends set with its own caps and timing. Switching it on, or raising a friends' limit, loosens the shocker rules: a Ctrl+Z that would do either asks first.

Each shocker's card has Allowed: Shock · Vibrate · Beep. One switched off is refused for that shocker, whoever sends it: your behaviours, your avatar's menu, friends, the web remote. Switching one off stops a running pulse or hold of it at once. An unarmed shock is a vibrate, so with Vibrate off it's refused as well. A behaviour that uses a switched-off action greys that shocker's chip. Friends see the button greyed, with why: "Shock is switched off on their side". Nothing switched off ever reaches the shocker. A shock that must be warned first, on a shocker with both Vibrate and Beep off, is held back there and logged: it can't warn.

When you, a friend and someone on your web remote hold one shocker at once, it plays the strongest hold steadily. A shock always wins over a vibrate, whatever their strengths, and a vibrate over a beep. One of them letting go doesn't cut the others.

Stop all on the hub card (or On off on Home); the shocker's own On / Off; Off in the sidebar, or OGP/Off; Off while you're away; the USB cable coming out, and VRChat going silent; Pause all on the Friends page, for everything friends send.

ShockOSC is OpenShock's VRChat app. An avatar set up for it carries parameters starting with ShockOsc/, one group per shocker. OGP understands them: such an avatar needs one click, and you don't run ShockOSC itself.

Wear the avatar, with VRChat's OSC on. On the Shockers page, a card says Your avatar is set up for ShockOSC, with a row per group: what it becomes, and the shocker it drives. Each group takes the shocker with its name. Drop another shocker on its row to change that. _All takes every shocker. Press Set up N behaviours. The behaviours land with the others, each with a grey SHOCKOSC tag. Run the setup again after you change the avatar: it only adds what's missing. ShockOSC parameter Becomes ShockOsc/<Group> (a touch) a Contact that shocks once per touch _IShock / _IVibrate / _ISound a Contact that pulses once with that action _CShock / _CVibrate / _CSound a Continuous _IsGrabbed / _Stretch (a PhysBone) a Pull: vibrate while held, a shock on the let-go, as strong as the pull New behaviours start with the same values as a behaviour you add by hand (a Contact 20 for 0.5 s, a Continuous and a Pull 5 to 30), except that a touch shocks only once it has been held for 0.25 s, as in ShockOSC, so a brush does nothing. Change them like any other.

An avatar can carry ShockOSC's own settings (ShockOsc/_Config/…), often as radials in its menu. They and the behaviours keep the same values: change one in the avatar's menu and the behaviours change, shown on the page at once; change a behaviour on the page and the avatar's setting changes too. ShockOSC setting The behaviours' Intensity (or MaxIntensity in its range mode) Strength (a Continuous's and a Pull's top) MinIntensity (range mode) A Continuous's and a Pull's lowest strength Duration (or MaxDuration) Length CooldownTime Rest after a shock: after a shock from the group, its behaviours wait this long HoldTime A touch's Touch for at least Paused On / Off: Paused switches them off and stops at once whatever they're running, like Stop; it's sent once they're all off _All's settings are the ones every group follows, as in ShockOSC. A group goes with its own (ShockOsc/_Config/Collar/…) only when the avatar has them. So one Intensity radial moves every group's behaviours together, and changing one of them on the page changes the others with it. The avatar's Paused for _All is a kill switch: on, every ShockOSC behaviour goes off. When you switch avatars, OGP sends its values first. The avatar takes them, rather than OGP taking the avatar's saved ones. A friend with YOLO on can set these too, like your own menu. _NextIntensity / _NextDuration only ever make the next action gentler. Your limits and arming hold as always, whatever either side says: a strength of 80 on a shocker capped at 25 sends 25. A strength of 0 sends nothing.

OGP sends ShockOSC's feedback parameters back (Active, Cooldown, CooldownPercentage, DurationRemaining, Intensity, per group and _Any), so the avatar's lights and countdowns follow what the shockers really do. Only real shocks count: an unarmed shock is a vibrate and lights nothing. OGP's own Off while you're away stands in for ShockOSC's "disable while AFK".

OGP drives a bHaptics suit, sleeves, hands, feet or head straight over Bluetooth: no bHaptics Player, no pairing in Windows. It plays your avatar's bHaptics contacts, and OWO's too if you like. Switch it on first: Settings → Features → bHaptics — suit and sleeves over Bluetooth, or tick A bHaptics suit or sleeves in What are you here for?. It's off by default. Its page is Suits, shared with OWO and the haptic trackers. The Suits page: front and back, every bHaptics motor an orange dot, OWO's muscles purple patches, and a haptic tracker as a blue puck.

The Suits page is a body, front and back. Every bHaptics motor is an orange dot; OWO's muscles are purple patches around them; haptic trackers are blue pucks. Click a part of her to set it up: its card opens beside her, with a line to it. A click on empty space closes it. Press and hold a dot to feel it. Each card says whether the avatar you wear has that part's contacts. A dashed amber ring marks what's missing. Touches light up as they land.

Close the bHaptics Player. A suit takes one connection at a time. Switch the suit on. Press Connect on the bHaptics card. Connect when the app starts does it every time from then on. Let go hands the suit back to the Player or a game.
You have lists the bHaptics parts: tick the ones you own. Only those show on her. A vest is ticked by default, and a part that connects ticks itself.

All of these work, with no setup: the official bHaptics avatar package (bOSC/v2…); older bHapticsOSC setups; with Also feel OWO's contacts on (the default), the OWO avatar package's contacts play the bHaptics motors around them. Zone routes send an SPS zone or one of your SPS Sources to a part of the body, for both suits: Add route, then its zone, type and gain.

If OGP stops sending, the suit goes quiet within a quarter of a second. Off, VRChat going silent, Off while away and the suit's own anti-stuck (its Anti-stuck card in the bHaptics frame, with its own times) hold the suit too. The OWO suit has its own in the OWO frame. Tell VRChat sends OGP/BHapticsConnected, and one per part. See "It's connected" parameters.

OGP drives an OWO suit through the My OWO app, the way a game does. My OWO keeps your calibration and drives the suit. Switch it on first: Settings → Features → OWO — EMS suit through the My OWO app, or tick An OWO suit in What are you here for?. It's off by default. It's on the Suits page, next to bHaptics. OWO is EMS It moves your muscles with electric pulses. OGP caps everything, and starts low: the Ceiling begins at 60 %.

Open My OWO and calibrate the suit there. Press Connect on the OWO card. OGP looks for My OWO on this PC first, then on your network. My OWO at takes an address if it's elsewhere. Connect when the app starts is off by default: OWO connects only when you press Connect, until you switch that on.

100 % is the top of your calibration in My OWO. Ceiling caps every sensation. It starts at 60 %, and can't go past what you set. Each muscle has its own Top. Frequency sets the pulse frequency. Stop all stops OWO at once and refuses everything until Resume. Off, VRChat going silent, Off while away and quitting OGP stop it too. Its own anti-stuck, the Anti-stuck card in the OWO frame, cuts a contact that freezes, with its own times. Being EMS, keep it on unless you know why not.

The OWO avatar package's contacts (owo_suit_…) work with no setup. With Also feel bHaptics' contacts on (the default), a bHaptics contact plays the OWO muscle around it. Tell VRChat sends OGP/OWOConnected while OGP is connected to My OWO.

A SteamVR tracker with a motor can buzz from your avatar's contacts: a Vive Tracker with a Haptic Pancake on its pins, a Tundra with a Tundra Tapper, or a controller set up as a tracker. Switch it on first: Settings → Features → Trackers — vibrating trackers through SteamVR, or tick Trackers that vibrate in What are you here for?. It's off by default. OGP never starts SteamVR itself.

Trackers sit on Haptic Pancake's nine spots, and each spot follows Haptic Pancake's parameter name by default. So an avatar set up for Haptic Pancake works as it is. Spot Parameter Head HapticHead Chest HapticChest Hips HapticHips Right elbow, Left elbow HapticElbowRight, HapticElbowLeft Right knee, Left knee HapticKneeRight, HapticKneeLeft Right foot, Left foot HapticFootRight, HapticFootLeft A spot can follow several parameters: the strongest wins.

A tracker goes where its role in SteamVR's Manage Trackers puts it, as a blue puck on the Suits page's body. A tracker without a usable role is listed under the chips with Buzz (to find which one it is) and Place on her: the next click on a spot puts it there.

Each spot's Top starts at 80 %: Haptic Pancake's guide warns that a plain motor overloads the Vive Tracker's pin at full. A level that isn't sent again soon plays nothing. Off, VRChat going silent, Off while away and the trackers' own anti-stuck (under her, after the trackers, with its own times) hold the trackers like the suits. Only real trackers buzz: never OGP's own toy entries in SteamVR, never virtual trackers.

Home is where OGP opens: a row for everything you have, with its quick switches. The details live on each device's own page. Click a row to open it there. Home's Devices: two connected toys, the shocker hub, the bHaptics and OWO suits, the PSVR2 headset, and a toy that's switched off, greyed at the bottom.

Until the basics work, the top of Home shows Toy on · VRChat connected · Avatar has SPS · Avatar menu, a dot each. It goes away once the first three are green. Don't show again folds it to one slim line for good, and Take the tour starts the guided tour.
Test all buzzes every connected toy gently for about a second.

Every toy you've connected gets a row, outlined in its own colour and numbered in the corner. The number is its place: toys keep the order they connected in, and friends see them in that order too. From left to right: Its name and a dot: green while connected. A toy you've used before but that's switched off stays listed, greyed, with OFFLINE. What drives it in the active mode: All SPS, a zone's name, or how many zones. The four chips: Touch from Self / Others, Penetration from Self / Others. A chip sets that choice on every chain of the toy, in the active mode. It shows half lit while the toy's chains disagree; a click makes them all agree. A chip greys out when none of the toy's chains hears that kind. Sleep over Anti-stuck: Sleep puts just this toy to sleep (three full strokes wake it); Anti-stuck, on by default, can leave this one toy out. See Anti-stuck and Sleep. Battery, and a live meter per motor. Mute silences this one toy. Test buzzes it. In a wide window it's all one line: the name, then the chips as two rows, Touch above Penetration with Sleep over Anti-stuck beside them, then the battery, meters, Mute and Test. Only when the window gets narrower do the zones and chips move to a line under the name, and in a narrow one the battery and meters get a line of their own too.

Arm shocks, Share with friends and On, with red words that say Shocks armed or Shocks not armed. These are the same switches as on the Shockers page: flip one and the other follows. Arming asks first. See Arming and limits. In a narrow window Arm shocks and Share with friends move to a line under the name; On stays at the end. The shocker hub's row: PiShock with two shockers, armed, shared with friends, and on.
The bHaptics and OWO suits each have On and Also feel OWO's contacts / Also feel bHaptics' contacts. The PSVR2 headset has On. See Suits and trackers and PSVR2.

The sidebar shows the same things on every page: the four mode buttons, Total output strength, Off and Sleep, then the pages, then whether VRChat and Intiface are connected. See Modes, strength, Off and Sleep.
The top of the sidebar is the same on every page: four mode buttons, Total output strength, Off and Sleep. The four modes (Combined is active), total output strength at 70 %, Off and Sleep.

A mode is a routing: which parts of your avatar drive which motors. It isn't how strong anything is. There are four, and one is active at a time: Combined: every socket feeding one motor. Separate: each socket driving its own motor. Custom 1 and Custom 2: anything in between. Right-click a mode to rename it or change its icon. Each mode keeps its own copy of every motor's Input stage: its zones, its parameters, who it hears, and its mirror to VRChat. Everything else is shared: the feel of every chain, each toy's output gain and range, the strength. So you tune a toy once, and a mode only changes how it's wired. Remember mode per avatar (Settings → Modes) switches to the mode each avatar last used when you put it on. From VRChat, OGP/Mode (0 to 3) switches modes. See The avatar menu.

One multiplier on everything your toys get. It never touches your tuning, so turning it back up gives you exactly the feel you had. From VRChat it's OGP/Strength. If one toy always feels stronger than the rest, leave the slider alone and trim that toy instead: Toys → the toy → its chain → Output → Gain. If a motor does nothing until well up its range, or gets unpleasant near the top, set Output → Range to the part it really uses. Both hold in every mode.

Panic silence. Everything stops at once, whatever the slider says: toys, shockers, suits, trackers, the headset and friends' drives. Switch it back off and your level returns untouched. While you're AFK in VRChat, OGP holds the same Off for you without touching your switch. See Off while away.

Makes every toy hard to wake. Every chain's Wake stage switches to counting strokes: nothing plays until three full strokes land within six seconds. A brush against a sleeping partner does nothing. Your own Wake settings come straight back when you switch Sleep off. Buttplug toys only. Each toy's bar has a Sleep chip of its own, for that toy alone. While the sidebar's Sleep is on, every toy's chip is lit. See Anti-stuck and Sleep. note Off and Sleep aren't remembered when you restart OGP, on purpose: starting in silence, or in a sleep nobody remembers switching on, looks like a broken app.

VRChat only sends a value when it changes. If a contact stops updating (you swap avatar, your partner leaves, the link drops), its last value would keep a toy, a suit or the headset running. Anti-stuck notices a value that has frozen and stops it. It's on by default. Each kind of device has its own anti-stuck, with its own switch and times, on its own page, because they may want different settings: Device Where Your toys The Toys page, under Toy server. Each toy's bar has its own switch too. The bHaptics suit The Suits page, the bHaptics frame's Anti-stuck card. The OWO suit The Suits page, the OWO frame's Anti-stuck card. Haptic trackers The Suits page, under her, after the trackers. The PSVR2 headset The PSVR2 page, at the bottom of the Contact card. The Toys page: anti-stuck for every toy, under Toy server.

A real contact between zero and one never holds perfectly still: animation and IK jitter it all the time. So: Frozen part-way: stop after (1 s by default): a value that stops moving somewhere in the middle is cut quickly. Held at 100%: ease off after (10 s by default): all the way in and held is a real state, so it gets the longer wait, then eases off over 3 s. A new value brings it back at once. The times are sliders, from 1 s to 10 minutes; they hide while the switch is off. Each suit has its own, in its frame on the Suits page. If you updated from an older OGP, each one starts with the switch and times you had: before, one anti-stuck in Settings covered them all.

Each toy's bar, on Home and on the Toys page, has two chips beside Touch and Penetration: Sleep puts just this toy to sleep: nothing from your avatar's contacts plays on it until three full strokes land within six seconds, so a brush against a sleeping partner does nothing. After 45 seconds without a stroke it sleeps again. While the sidebar's Sleep is on, every toy sleeps and every chip is lit (and greyed). Like the sidebar's, it isn't remembered when you restart OGP. Friends' drives still reach a sleeping toy. Anti-stuck is on for every toy by default. Switch it off for a toy that should keep playing a value that sits still. It only counts while the Toys page's anti-stuck is on (greyed while that is off), and it's remembered, the same in every mode. A toy's row: the Touch and Penetration chips, then Sleep over Anti-stuck. Ctrl+Z asks first before it would switch an anti-stuck off or make it wait longer, as doing it by hand would.

Settings' Safety card (called Toy Safety before) holds Off while you're away: while VRChat says you're AFK, everything is off. See Off while away. Above it, a button for each page with an anti-stuck takes you there. Settings → Safety: buttons to each device's anti-stuck, and Off while you're away.
Off in the sidebar, or OGP/Off from your avatar's menu. Mute on a toy's row silences that one toy. OGP's Test pulses (Test all, a toy's Test, OGP/Test) are gentle: about 20 % for a moment.
documents.s: Other things that stop your toys

documents.t: OGP talks to toys through a toy server: Intiface, the Buttplug.io engine. Built in (the default): OGP runs Intiface for you, on this PC. Nothing else to install or start. Your own Intiface Central: on this PC, or on a phone or another PC on the same network. Use it when your toys are paired with Intiface Central on your phone. The Toys page's Toy server line, and the sidebar's Intiface row, say which one OGP uses and whether it's connected. The Toys page's Toy server line: connected, built in, on this PC.

On the phone, open Intiface Central (3.0 or newer) and switch on Listen on all network interfaces. Also switch on Broadcast Server Info via mDNS (under Show Advanced/Experimental Settings). Then OGP finds the phone by itself. Start the server on the phone, and keep the app open while you play. In OGP: Settings → Intiface Engine → switch off Use built-in Intiface engine. Leave Address empty and OGP looks on this PC and your network until one answers. Or type the phone's address, like 192.168.1.50 (add :port if you changed Intiface's Server Port). The line under the address says when it's connected: ✓ Connected to … at …. Finding a phone without an address needs Intiface Central 3.1. Switching between built in and your own reconnects by itself. info With your own Intiface Central, Intiface's own device list applies. The built-in engine leaves one entry out, so it never takes a Bluetooth serial device (a MeshCore radio, an ESP32 board) for a toy.
documents.s: Use Intiface Central on a phone

documents.t: Home shows each toy at a glance. The Toys page, right under Friends in the sidebar, holds everything about them: each toy's signal chains, the toy server, SPS Sources and the tuning tools. The Toys page: Scan now, the Toy server line, anti-stuck, and a card per toy, folded to its one row. SPS Sources and Tuning tools are folded at the bottom.

OGP looks for toys by itself: every few seconds while no toy is connected, every 30 seconds while one is. Scan now looks right away, for a toy you just switched on. Beside it, OGP says when it looks next.
Whether the toy server is CONNECTED and where it runs: built in, on this PC, or your own Intiface Central. Intiface settings opens Settings → Intiface Engine. See Where your toys connect.
Under Toy server: anti-stuck for every toy, with its two times. It stops a toy whose contact has frozen. Each toy's bar has its own Anti-stuck chip to leave one toy out. See Anti-stuck and Sleep.

A card's bar is the same as the toy's row on Home: the four chips, Sleep and Anti-stuck, battery, meters, Mute and Test. Every card starts folded to that bar, one row per toy. Click the bar to open the card on each motor's chains, each folded to one bar: its name, a letter per stage lit by its live level, and its settings at a glance. Click a chain to open it. Another click on the toy's bar folds the whole card away again. A click on the toy's row on Home opens its card here. A toy's chain opened: Chain 1 of its motor, from Input through Depth, Speed and Punch, Combine, Wake and Envelope to Zero cut and Output.

Each motor has a signal chain: the stages that turn your avatar's contacts into the motor's level. Click a stage to edit it. Rest the mouse on a stage to see what each knob does. Stage What it does Input Where the signal comes from: which zones, touch or penetration, from you or from others. Depth How deep or close the contact is: the steady part of the feel. Speed How fast the contact moves: the lively part. It fades once movement stops. Punch A short hit on top of a fast thrust in (or pull out), then it decays. Combine How Depth and Speed merge: Max (the louder wins, the default), Add or Multiply. Wake Nothing plays until there's real contact. Strokes mode waits for full strokes, which is what Sleep uses. Envelope How the level moves over time: smoothing, and an optional texture so a steady hold feels alive. Zero cut Snaps to silence the moment the contact is gone, instead of fading out. Off by default. Output A gain to balance this toy against the others, and the range the toy can use. A motor can have up to six chains. + Add chain adds one that runs on the same input. A chain can be for Penetration, Touch or Custom; a coloured bar on its fold row says which. Reset to defaults puts a chain's feel back to OGP's own.

Open its chain, then click Input. Click Select Zones. These are your SPS sources: All SPS hears every SPS zone your avatar has. Or switch on only the ones you want: the zones VRChat reports for the avatar you wear, and the ones you built under SPS Sources. Who it hears: Touch from yourself, Touch from others, Penetration from yourself, Penetration from others. They're the same four as the chips on the toy's bar. The zones are kept per mode. The feel isn't: you tune it once.

+ Add Variable, in a chain's Input stage, maps any OSC parameter to the motor. The motor follows the loudest of them, plus its zones. The picker hides what's rarely wanted: VRChat's own parameters, GoGo Loco, face tracking, VRCFury's internals, physics assets, PhysBone states, OGP's own and SPS's. Each group is a chip with its count at the top of the picker. A lit chip hides its group, and Show everything shows them all. A search also finds hidden ones, under Hidden by filters. A parameter you already mapped is never hidden.

One small line, after every motor's chains: Avatar parameters is folded, and says how many are on. Open it for: Mirror to VRChat parameter, one per motor (named by its motor when the toy has several). It sends the motor's level (0 to 1) back to your avatar, for a glow or a fill meter. Type the name, or Pick… one your avatar sends. Tell VRChat while this toy is connected, a Bool, on by default. See "It's connected" parameters. Delete device, at the right end, forgets the toy and everything set up for it, in every mode. Switch it on again and it comes back as a new toy.
documents.s: At the bottom of the card

documents.t: Your own zones, built from raw VRChat contact receivers: for spots the standard SPS zones don't cover, or an avatar without them. Each source is a zone you can pick in any toy's Input stage, like your avatar's own. A source combines: Proximity: one or more proximity receivers. The loudest wins. Activation: on/off contacts. The proximity only counts while one of them fires. Leave it empty for no gate. Velocity: on-enter contacts. While one fires, the level is multiplied by Velocity ×. Max value: a cap on the proximity before the multiplier. Type the contact names separated by commas. The /avatar/parameters/ prefix is optional. Sources are shared by every mode.
For when you shape how a toy responds: the input simulator: a stroke to tune against, without a partner; the signal graph of one chain. The fold remembers whether you left it open.

A chime plays when a toy connects (going up) or disconnects (going down). Settings → Connection Settings → Sound when a toy connects or disconnects switches it off, with its volume beside it. Show toys in SteamVR (Settings, on by default, Windows only) lists your connected toys in SteamVR's device strip with their battery. Just for show: they can never be picked up as trackers. Switching it off takes them out of SteamVR again. A PC without SteamVR is never touched.
